title: Conversational capacity ledger and pricing sketches
body:
Quick personal ledger for an alternative pricing idea: charge for conversational capacity instead of raw tokens only. Goal: create a predictable SDK-friendly plan for chat apps where concurrency and tail latency (KV cache misses) drive cost more than steady token volume.

Premise and motivations:
- Observed: customer X (pilot) has high token counts but very predictable patterns (many short sessions). Customer Y has fewer tokens but lots of concurrency spikes and high kv-cache miss rates -> more infra cost.
- Current per-token pricing hides mismatch: high concurrencies impose scheduling overhead and reduce batching efficiency.
- Idea: introduce a capacity/credit layer that prices the ability to sustain concurrent conversational sessions (session-seconds) + a token surcharge for very long tails.

Definitions / variables (back-of-envelope):
- avg_turn_tokens = 55 (typical short chat turn)
- avg_turns_per_session = 6 -> avg_tokens_per_session = 330
- session_duration_active = 45s (user-facing time window when request is expected)
- avg_requests_per_session = 6 (one request per turn)
- concurrency_coefficient (C) = fraction of sessions concurrently active at any moment (for multi-user scenarios pick 0.02 for baseloads, spikes up to 0.2)
- kv_cache_hit_rate = 0.75 baseline, can drop to 0.4 for many unique prompts
- batching_efficiency = 0.7 for normal load, down to 0.4 during spikes

Infra cost anchors (approx):
- GPU-hour price (amortized infra + ops) = $6.5/hr (p50 internal blended)
- effective tokens/sec a single GPU can serve (with quantized Llama-like model @ 8-bit) = 20k tokens/sec sustained, but real-world throughput after latency constraints ~ 6k tokens/sec for small-turn interactive workloads (accounting for small batch inefficiency)
- tokens per GPU-hour at real workload = 6k * 3600 = 21.6M tokens -> cost per 1M tokens = $6.5 / 21.6 = ~$0.30/M tokens (note: this is optimistic; long-tail prompts and cache misses increase per-token infra cost)

Capacity-centric pricing sketch A: session-capacity + token surcharge
- Unit: 1 session-capacity unit (SCU) = ability to hold 1 concurrent active session for 1 hour (session-second basis: 3600 session-seconds)
- Price target: aim for 3x infra margin at base usage. If base infra cost to hold 1 concurrent session (calc below) = $0.02/hr -> SCU list price = $0.06/hr
- Backcalc: cost to hold 1 concurrent session: avg_tokens_per_session * requests_per_session * (session_rate factor) -> easier: we estimate GPU can sustain 6k tokens/sec -> cost per active-session-second = (avg_turn_tokens * avg_turns_per_session) / tokens/sec / 3600 * GPU_hour_price -> plug numbers: (330 tokens) / 6000 tokens/sec = 0.055s of GPU time per session (this indicates many sessions are multiplexed because of short bursts) -> that looks like I messed units. Recompute properly below.

Recompute carefully (session-level GPU time):
- Each session generates 330 tokens across ~6 requests. For each request, assume a latency-limited service where each request needs ~50ms of GPU time on average (small-ish model, KV cache hit). So gpu_time_per_request = 0.05s -> gpu_time_per_session = 6 * 0.05 = 0.3s GPU time per session.
- GPU cost per second = $6.5 / 3600 = $0.001806/second. So cost per session = 0.3 * 0.001806 = $0.00054 (about $0.0005). If we think of capability to support 1 concurrent session for 1 hour: that corresponds to 3600 / 0.3 = 12k sessions per GPU-hour (approx). So cost per concurrent-session-hour = GPU-hour cost / (12k) = $6.5 / 12k = $0.00054 (matches per session cost times sessions/hour).
- So infra cost to reserve 1 concurrent session-hour ~= $0.00054. This is far lower than earlier naive $0.02; that's OK because interactive sessions are very cheap in steady-state when requests are small; spikes and cold starts blow that up.

Pricing implication: we can set SCU price = $0.005/hr (about 9x infra) as a durable commitment price (for low friction tier) and $0.02/hr for burstable on-demand. Alternatively, pack as monthly packs: e.g., 10k SCU-hours monthly for $35 (equiv $0.0035/hr).

Token surcharge:
- Keep token price but lower headline price: tokens priced at $0.18 per 1M for baseline (to encourage high-volume customers to commit on SCUs). For cache-miss heavy workloads, surcharge kicks in: if kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.5 then tokens price doubles for those requests (or +100% surcharge) to reflect higher infra/time cost. Implementation: track tokens by request tag: cache_hit vs cache_miss.

Tier sketches (customer-facing):
- Free: 20 SCU-hours / month + 50k tokens free. (good for small dev testing).
- Starter: 1,000 SCU-hours/month + 15M tokens -> $9/mo (anchor low price).
- Team: 15k SCU-hours/month + 250M tokens -> $99/mo
- Business: 150k SCU-hours/month + 2.5B tokens -> $899/mo
- Enterprise: custom reserved SCU capacity + commit discounts + SLA
Notes: these numbers intentionally cheap on SCU to make product stickier. Must run unit-econ sim.

Unit-econ quick sim (very rough):
- If typical paying Starter customer uses SCU-hours at 20% utilization of their purchased capacity => in practice they consume 200 SCU-hours -> infra cost = 200 * 0.00054 = $0.108 -> tokens cost ~= (15M tokens * $0.18 / 1M) = $2.7 -> total infra + token DC cost ~ $2.8 -> list price $9 -> gross margin ~ 69% before S&M and support. Seems viable for small.
- For Team tier: utilization 40% -> 6k SCU consumed -> infra = 6k * 0.00054 = $3.24 -> tokens 250M * 0.18 = $45 -> total cost $48.24 -> price $99 -> margin ~ 51%. Acceptable.

Risks and edge cases:
- Very chatty long-context sessions (1000+ tokens per turn) break this model: per-session GPU time increases linearly and our SCU unit underprices them. Need to add per-request long-tail surcharge: any request > 1000 tokens charged extra tokens at 2x base.
- Cold-starts: private deployments with tiny fleets will have higher per-session cost; offer dedicated/private pricing separately.
- Metering complexity: tracking SCU-hours accurately with ephemeral websockets and retries is tricky; need robust session semantics (open/close pulses) and fallback on request-count-based billing if session telemetry missing.

Implementation TODOs (tech notes):
- define session lifecycle events in SDK (session-open, session-heartbeat, session-close) and standard TTL of 60s after last heartbeat.
- make telemetry robust to offline clients and browser tab suspends (use server-side perception of concurrency when in doubt).
- tag requests with cache-hit boolean for token-surcharge accounting (reference: /observability/telemetry-telemetry plan)
- build internal unit-econ sim (Jupyter) to sample different avg_turn_tokens, kv_cache_hit_rate, concurrency_coefficient and produce expected margin curves. Link to PRJ-3842 for initial spec.

Questions / open knobs:
- Should SCU be sold in monthly packs, or per-app active-seat? Monthly packs feel easy for finance and commitment.
- What price anchor makes the tradeoff between encouraging commit vs converting high-velocity payg customers?
- Legal/contracting: are there complications attaching SCU to API keys vs orgs? likely tie to org-level billing.

Notes to self: run sim across 1000 random customer profiles (sampled from telemetry) to find 20th/50th/80th percentile consumption curves. Also compare against pure per-token revenue. Put results into a short deck for Pricing review (cc: Diego).

Random brain dump comparisons to other models:
- Compared to plain tokens: this model favors interactive apps with small-turn sessions (lower token price) and penalizes concurrency-heavy bursty apps unless they buy SCUs.
- Compared to seat-based: SCU is more flexible for bots where an "end user" count is fuzzy (sessions map better than seats).

End of ledger. Will iterate after running unit-econ sim.

-- Maya
